Breakfast and After School Clubs
School Life
Breakfast and After School Clubs
Additional Support for Parents and Carers
At Julian's, we understand the needs of busy parents and carers, therefore offer both morning and after-school wrap around care in addition to our sports and special interest clubs.
We offer a range of clubs, before and after school, run by outside professionals. These include drama, science, art, dance, table tennis, animation, photography, forest school, choir, coding, capoeira, football, netball, dodgeball, multi-sports and summer sports. Most clubs have strict limits on numbers and also a small fee to cover the costs of staffing and resources.
Morning Club
A Morning Club is held every morning in the library resource area of the school from 8:30-8:55am. The service is on a drop-in basis at a charge of £2.00 per session. It is proving highly popular with a large number of regulars attending each day.
Wrap Around Care
Schoolfriend Clubs Ltd is an external organisation offering wrap around care at both the Streatham and West Norwood sites for all JPS pupils: Breakfast Club (breakfast included). From 7.45am - £4.75 per child After school Club (snack included) – Until 6.00pm - £11.00 per child (siblings £10.50) Annual membership (per family) - £25.00 a year For further information parents/carers should visit the website: www.schoolfriendclub.com or email at: office@schoolfriendclub.com or phone: 0844 272 7158
Special Interest Clubs
Our special interest clubs take place on both sites and include:
When joining a club it is essential that your child attends regularly and also informs the school if they are going to miss the activity. The school will always aim to inform you by 1pm if a club is cancelled. Letters are sent out at the start of each term to inform you of the costs for clubs and activities.
Drama Club with Boo Theatre
Dance Club with WhizzDance
Art with Little House of Holly
Science Club with Mother Nature Science
Animation with London Lens Project
Forest School with Forries Education
Table Tennis with B Dynamic Sport
Coding Club with Blue Shift Coding
Choir Club with Florence and Izzy
Capoeira with Danca Da Liberdade Capoeira School
Yoga and Mindfulness with Holliestic Wellbeing
Sports Clubs
Sport4Learning offer a series of clubs on both the Streatham and West Norwood sites. Clubs include multi-sports, summer sports, netball and football plus specialist squads for Year 5 and 6 children.
Interventions
Due to the pandemic and its long term effects on children's learning, Julian’s may offer interventions in order to close the knowledge gaps.
For further information about after-school clubs please contact Rebecca rcolman@juliansprimary.org.uk.

PTFA (Parents, Teachers and Friends Association)
Get Involved
PTFA (Parents, Teachers and Friends Association)
Why join our PTFA?
Support the school
The PTFA is vital to the success of Julian’s. Be part of the group that pays for the playground your child loves or funds extra art supplies that spark imaginations.
It’s totally flexible
Whether you’re a full-time parent or working the nine to five, anyone can get involved. It’s less commitment than you think. Small jobs such as organising uniforms, promoting events or clearing coffee cups keep everything running smoothly.
Make friendships
Meet and chat to a wider circle of families from different classes and year groups. Get to know other parents, and bond over events, socials and get-togethers.
Be better connected
Create closer links with the teachers and staff. If you’re new to the school, the PTFA is an excellent way to find out how things work.
Change school for the better
Have a say on important decisions. Work with the school and other parents to see where improvements can be made and help implement them. Directly influence the experienceof your child and hundreds of others.
Impact your child’s learning
Studies show that children whose parents and carers are involved in their education do better in school and our PTFA benefits equally from active parents/carers.
Everyone is welcome
It’s important to have mums, dads and carers represented. We all bring different skills and different perspectives.
Create lasting memories
Our children are only at school for a few years, but they will remember the difference we make for a lifetime. They will cherish the activities we fund, learn using resources we buy,and remember the events we put on. Help keep the PTFA going so future students can benefit too.
PTFA Newsletter
What is the PTFA?
Julian's Primary PTFA is a social group of parents and carers who fundraise for school resources and activities. We work closely with the school to benefit the pupils. Every parent, carer and staff member is automatically a member and we encourage everyone to get involved.
The group is run by an elected executive comprising volunteer parents, carers and staff and they hold regular meetings and coffee mornings at both sites. It updates the whole school community through their fortnightly newsletter and via a team of dedicated Class Reps. The group has charitable status and its primary aim is to raise valuable funds for the school. Everyone is welcome to contribute ideas, time, energy and enthusiasm!
What has the PTFA provided in recent years?
Year 6 end-of-year event, yearbook and t-shirts
School values mosaics
IT equipment including laptops and cameras
Funds towards the gardening project
Theatre visits for the children
Playground markings to support learning
How do we raise money?
Regular events have been school discos, cake sales, winter and summer fairs & raffles and social events for adults, for example the infamous quiz night!
How can you help?
Help at a disco; make or sell cakes; run a stall at one of the fairs; help with our Facebook page; donate gifts for raffles; ask your business to sponsor an event; ask your company to match funds raised; design or print posters; bring fresh ideas....
Everyone can help raise funds when shopping online. When you shop online, please consider signing up to Easyfundraising to support Julian's Primary School PTFA.
It’s a really easy way to raise money for the school – you just use the easyfundraising site to shop online with more than 3,300 well known online stores like Amazon, Argos, John Lewis, ASOS, Booking.com, eBay, Boden, and M&S and when you make a purchase, the retailer sends the PTFA a donation, at no extra cost to you.
We want to raise as much as possible, so please visit our new easyfundraising page at https://www.easyfundraising.org.uk/causes/juliansptfa/ and click ‘support this cause’.
How do I get involved?
The Julian's PTFA reflects the warm, friendly and inclusive ethos of the school and we hope that you will be actively involved. Either come to a meeting, email us at juliansptfa@googlemail.com and ‘like’ us on facebook http://www.facebook.com/JuliansPrimarySchoolPTFA.
We are also looking to recruit Class Reps so that we have 1 or 2 contacts per class so that we can share news with all parents and garner support for events. We also have several positions open on the Committee.
Please email Olivia Foxon on ofoxon@juliansprimary.org.uk if you are interested in being a Class Rep or getting involved in the Committee.

Special Educational Needs or Disabilities (SEND)
We understand that all children are individuals and their journeys will be unique. We take a holistic approach, teaching a creative, inclusive and enriched curriculum that helps every child reach his or her potential.
Children with Special Educational Needs or Disabilities (SEND) are highly valued and respected at Julian's and are supported by dedicated, skilled and motivated teachers and support staff.
We are excited to have introduced new learning spaces at Julian’s. These two new intervention classes provide specialist teaching to a group of children in Years 1 & 2 in West Norwood and Years 3 & 4 in Streatham.
We are committed to meeting the needs of every pupil at the school and have high expectations of all pupils whatever their needs and abilities. The introduction of these specialist teaching spaces is part of our ongoing commitment to providing a tailored education that meets the unique requirements of each and every one of our pupils.
We believe that this initiative will not only benefit the children directly involved but will also contribute to a more inclusive and supportive learning environment for all children across the school.
“This is a school that recognises the importance of children feeling happy and confident within themselves to be able to learn effectively.” - Inclusion Quality Mark, Centre of Excellence, January 2020
What We Do
Special Educational Needs or Disabilities (SEND)
What different types of support are available for a child with SEND at Julian’s Primary School?
There is a graduated approach to SEND at Julian’s Primary School with three different levels of support for children with additional needs:
1. Quality first teaching by class teacher
2. Targeted interventions
3. Specialist interventions or groups run by outside agencies e.g. Speech and Language Therapy, Educational Psychology, Specialist Literacy support, and Occupational Therapy.
School staff with specific responsibilities for SEND
At Julian's, we have an Inclusion Manager who assists the Executive Headteacher and Heads of School in determining the strategic development of SEND policy and provision in the school. Our Inclusion Manager is also responsible for the effective leadership, organisation and management of inclusion and inclusive practice and in developing a clear, distinctive vision for inclusion both now and in the future. Please contact inclusion@juliansprimary.org.uk.
In addition to our Inclusion Manager, we have a Wellbeing Team, Learning Mentors and Sensory Rooms on both sites. We work hard to ensure that a child’s individual challenges are addressed and monitored so that every child makes progress, both academically and emotionally.

Nursery Admissions
Thank you for choosing Julian's Primary. Our Nursery is a very nurturing, self-contained space within our West Norwood site where children feel settled, happy and safe, whilst beginning to develop their learning and independence. There is no Nursery provison at our Streatham site.
For our September 2026 nursery intake, will be offering a combination of full-time and part-time, term-time only places. This is in response to feedback from our community and to make it easier for working families. We will be offering three types of place:
Key Info
Nursery Admissions
How much will it cost?
All 3- and 4-year-old children are entitled to 15 hours of funded term-time childcare. Some working parents are able to claim an additional 15 hours of funded childcare, allowing for 30 hours in total. To check your eligibility and receive your code, please visit the Government website. If you are not eligible for the 30 hour code for full time places, a top up fee will apply. There will also be the option for children to attend for extended hours 8:30am-9 and 3-3:30pm for an additional cost of £10 per hour.
Full time place if eligible for 30 hour code
Monday to Friday 9am – 3pm = 30 hours per week.
No additional costs.
Full time place if not eligible for 30 hour code
Monday to Friday 9am – 3pm = 30 hours per week.
15 hours free. 15 hours at £10 per hour.
Total to pay: £150 per week
Monday, Tuesday 9am – 3pm and Wednesday 9am – 12pm =15 hours per week
Wednesday 12pm – 3pm, Thursday and Friday 9am – 3pm = 15 hours per week
No additional costs.
There is no change to our admissions criteria. Nursery places will continue to be offered in the order detailed in the school’s nursery admissions policy.
Is there an option for extended hours?
There will be the option for full time children to attend for extended hours 8:30am-9 and 3-3:30pm. These are outside of the 30 hours and are provided at a cost of £10 per hour. This is an additional cost of £50 per week for full time places. Extended hours will also be available to part time places at the same rate of £10 per hour.
What will happen at lunch?
Children will bring their own lunch from home every day. A healthy snack in the form of a piece of fruit will be provided. Fresh water is always available.
Will wraparound care be available?
Yes, it will be possible to book wraparound care through our current provider, School Friend Club. They will have a separate early years room for Nursery and Reception children with appropriate adult-to-child ratios. This will be available until 6pm daily. There may also be the option for early drop off from 7:45am to give families greater flexibility if there is demand. Please enquire directly to School Friend Club for pricing structure.
Can I come and see the Nursery before applying?
We are delighted to invite prospective families to come and visit our West Norwood site by appointment only. We look forward to welcoming you to Julian's!
How do I apply for a Nursery place?
Children start Nursery in the academic year (September to August) that they have their 4th birthday. The closing date for applications for September 2026 places is 31st March 2026.
To apply, please download the Julian's Primary Nursery application form below and send the completed form to admissions@juliansprimary.org.uk.
On the form, you will be asked for your preference of a full-time or part time (session 1 or session 2) place. If you need any help filling out the form or have any questions, please call the School Office on 020 8761 1894 or email admissions@juliansprimary.org.uk and we will be happy to help. Places are offered according to our Nursery Admissions Policy available above.
What if I missed the deadline for a Nursery place?
You can put in an application after the deadline and be added to the waiting list. The waiting list is kept in order of the admissions criteria so you may not automatically be at the bottom. As places become available, we will contact you to offer you a place.
Please note: Children who are currently in Julians' Primary Nursery are not automatically offered a place in Reception. Parents/Carers of current Nursery pupils should follow the application process for Reception.

Lead Partner (formerly School Direct) Programme
Julian's Primary School has been directly involved with training teachers for over 15 years. We work as part of the Dunraven School Sharing Excellence Partnership to deliver high quality teacher training. Our training provider is Roehampton University.
Trainee teachers are placed with our experienced teachers and receive excellent support and mentoring from leaders in school. They can work in any Key Stage and across both of our sites. We have taken an active role in designing a training programme which draws on the talents of teachers at Julian's Primary School. We have invested heavily in the Lead Partner programme (formerly School Direct) and we are confident of providing a high quality, well-supported programme for existing and prospective students. We have a number of trained mentors who work together to ensure excellent professional and pastoral support for our students. Currently, around 50% of our teachers have trained through the programme at Julian's; the School Direct programme has enabled us to nurture our own teachers and leaders of the future. If you would like to find out more about training to be a teacher with us, please visit the Sharing Excellence Partnership website using the link below: https://www.sharingexcellence.org.uk/
Through this link and conversations with the Sharing Excellence co-ordinator, you are able to apply and also specify a preferred training location. Applications run throughout the year but early interest is encouraged to ensure schools have training spaces available.
If you would like a tour of Julian's Primary School, or you have any questions about training with us through the Sharing Excellence Partnership, please contact Dan Baumber at dbaumber@juliansprimary.org.uk to arrange a visit.

Rights Respecting School
Julian’s Primary School is committed to being a Rights Respecting School. The journey takes the participants through bronze, silver and gold accreditations.
The Rights Respecting Schools Award is granted to schools that show commitment to promoting and realising children’s rights. These rights are learned, taught, practised, respected, protected and promoted. Young people and the school community learn about children’s rights by putting them into practice every day. At Julian’s, we have been accredited the Silver award for our work so far.
The Silver award is achieved by taking a deeper look and embedding the Conventions of the Rights of the Child into policy, practice and culture of our school.
What We Do
Rights Respecting School
Our Right of the Week
WHAT IS A RIGHTS RESPECTING SCHOOL?
The UN convention consists of 54 articles in total, with each article referring to a right. UNICEF uses the UNCRC as a framework for its work for all the world’s children and has developed the Rights Respecting School Award (RRSA).
The UNICEF UK Rights Respecting Schools Award (RRSA) is based on principles of equality, dignity, respect, non-discrimination and participation. The RRSA seeks to put the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child at the heart of a school’s ethos and culture to improve well-being and develop every child to enable them to reach their full potential.
The UK Committee for UNICEF works with schools in the UK to create safe and inspiring places to learn, where children are respected, their talents are nurtured, and they are able to thrive.
The Rights Respecting Schools Award embeds these values in daily school life and gives children the best chance to lead happy, healthy lives and to be responsible, active citizens.

Cookies
Some cookies are necessary in order to make this website function correctly. These are set by default and whilst you can block or delete them by changing your browser settings, some functionality such as being able to log in to the website will not work if you do this. The necessary cookies set on this website are as follows:
Website CMS
A 'sessionid' token is required for logging in to the website and a 'crfstoken' token is used to prevent cross site request forgery. An 'alertDismissed' token is used to prevent certain alerts from re-appearing if they have been dismissed. An 'awsUploads' object is used to facilitate file uploads.
Matomo
We use Matomo cookies to improve the website performance by capturing information such as browser and device types. The data from this cookie is anonymised.
reCaptcha
Cookies are used to help distinguish between humans and bots on contact forms on this website.
